title: TradingView: Write trade tracking dashboard
description: I want to create a dashboard in TradingView. I currently have a dashboard like this in FxPro or MT5 but want to try out TradingView. The function of the dashboards will be where I can input one or multiple transaction specific paramotors. Like the trade amount and by what date it must be closed, and then track the gains and losses on the traded amount. The results I would like to have exported to a CSV or excel file. Detailed description of dashboard: The dashboard will have three views. 1. A welcoming view 2. The data input view 3. The tracking view Dashboard first view: 1. Welcome message 2. Button you must click on that says Add Transactions Dashboard Second view: Trade date inputs 1. Buy or Sell the currency selection or toggle 2. Transaction closing date: Day, Month, Year inputs (Tab should allow to move on) 3. Transaction amount 4. Trade reference 5. Capture button 6. Import button. (Should be able to import from Excel the above detail for multiple transactions if at all possible in TradingView.) Dashboard third view: Trade tracking view 1. Message that says how may day left till closing of trade “ You want a lower/higher price. You have X days remaining” 2. Trade inputs as per second dashboard 3. Reference of trade 4. Currency pair being tracked 5. Capture rate. 6. Stoploss rate (default stoploss must be added to Chart at 10 cents lower than the capture rate. Buying or selling the currency must be taken into consideration. You should also be able to edit the stoploss rate) 7. Current spot rate 8. Bank rate. It should reflect the current sport rate but can be changed to reflect added costs of the bank to the current spot rate. ( default is set at 0.00) 9. Amount in Rands. This is the transaction amount in reflected in Rands 10. Gain/Loss. This is the difference between the capture sport rate and the current spot rate. Buttons 11. Edit Transaction. If you edit a transaction the original Capture rate should be kept. 12. Execute. Once execute button is pressed data needs to be saved to file. 13. Hide the dashboard button. Data that needs to be captured in the CSV or excel (via FTP or what ever) file if possible: 1. Transaction reference 2. Currency pair 3. Buy or Sell 4. Amount 5. Capture date 6. Capture time 7. Closing date 8. Capture rate 9. Stoploss rate 10. Spot rate at execution 11. Amount in Rands 12. Gain/Loss 13. Time waited since captured date and time 14. Closing date rate. (Closing date rate should be spot rate at 16:00 on the closing date. Should a transaction be closed earlier then this should still be tracked till original closing date. Only after this data is captured the transaction is closed.) 15. Market movement from capture spot rate till Closing date rate. 16. (How did the execution rate compared against what the market gave from the capture date till the closing date.) How much of market opportunity was captured. 17. Risk 18. Volatility measurement during trading window Multiple transaction view. Create a view where you can see the summaries of the multiplate transactions that is open. It should include. 1. Trade reference 2. Currency pair 3. Buy or sell 4. Amount in Rands 5. Closing date 6. Capture spot rate 7. Stoploss rate *can be edit 8. Gains / loss 9. Small view of the chart?

title: Excel VBA data processing and reporting
description: The excel spreadsheet will be protected by an NDA, so that can only be shared once a contract is signed. The requirements as a rough outline: Data consist of date/time, position coordinates, "KP values (Kilometer point), sensor data from a machine moving along a path. Spreadsheet shall give a graph showing sensor data vs position along the path. - Import multiple txt based files into Excel - Option to append more files to the dataset later if forgotten to import earlier - and re-sorted into the existing data. - Sort data based on KP / time. - Register (?) sections of continuous data, and make a table of dates, KP from, KP to, distance (depending on going on ascending or descending KP) for the whole dataset - Filter data to avoid duplicate KP values. Should have one reading/line per meter (0.001 KP) - Highlight any gaps in dataset (i.e. missing KP values). Present subsets of the gaps in a separate sheet, i.e. 10 lines leading up to the gap, and 10 following the gap, for operator to analyse easily in a graph. - Potentially have an option to interpolate the KP and position data in the gaps and keep sensor values same (alarm if there are "big" differences, use threshold values to define this). - Create QC graphs, dynamically - depending on how many data gaps there are. Update gap graphs if gaps are reprocessed and filled by interpolation, remove gap graph entirely if gap is filled by adding real data. Keep a QC table with info about ranges that have been interpolated. - Create a feature to adjust certain sensor values within a range to account for errors in calibration or readings. Cut and paste original ranges into a separate table and show as dashed line in the graph, and overlay a solid line with final data. Keep a table of ranges manipulated for QC. - Unless speed values are correctly logged in dataset, create a formula that calculates speed, and average speed. Need to take into account data going past midnight, and at times where machine has stopped, and restarted 2 days later etc, to avoid spikes in the data. - Create feature to export positions to a given format. - Add a column whereby user can add manual values based on KP, which then will be interpolated along the line - more details on this later A separate project could come from this, where data that has been processed in this sheet, is pushed to a database in the cloud, and accessed by multiple Excel instances in different locations to read and publish to client. To be discussed separately.

description: Member Splash is a fast growing SaaS platform that provides membership management tools to recreational facilities across the United States. We're looking to establish long term relationships with developers, either as full or part-time hires or for ongoing contract work. About Us: We run a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform that has doubled in size each of the last three years and now serves clients across the United States. While the back end is powered by WordPress the front end and dashboard largely use the REST API and Vue.js. We have also developed a number of custom WordPress plugins that we use internally and a few of those have been released publicly. REQUIRED SKILLS WordPress: You know WordPress in depth. You’ve dug into the core code and understand how it works. If you needed to modify a built-in REST response you could, or you know where to turn to figure it out. You write clean, well commented code that someone coming behind you would be able to easily follow. Vue.js / Vuex / Vue Router: All of our interfaces are built with (or being ported to) Vue. You understand Vue.js features, patterns and best practices. Good knowledge of vanilla javascript is helpful as well. UI Frameworks: You have solid experience with a UI framework like Bootstrap. We use Vuetify.js, a Material Design framework, so bonus if you’re already familiar with it. APIs — We’re steadily shifting all of our code to being API based and frequently build tools that leverage third party APIs like SendGrid, Authorize.net, Google, etc. Git — Solid understanding of a standard Git workflow: branch / pull request / merge. We don’t honestly often use Git’s more advanced commands but if you needed to revert to a prior commit you could. Composer — our PHP code is all object oriented and namespaced and we use autoloading to handle dependencies. Node — we use Vue-cli so you won’t often be working with Node directly but experience with it is definitely a plus. Webpack — automates all of the development and build processes. Linting, minifying, etc. A decent understanding of how to adjust Webpack configurations would be helpful. Grunt — we try to automate as many things as possible and a stack of handy Grunt tasks are part of that. The skills listed above don’t cover everything you’ll need in your toolbox and we don’t expect that you’ll necessarily have all of them right now. But you should feel comfortable with a majority of them and with your ability to pick up new skills as you go. The things listed above aren't a checklist of skills you need to already have. They're examples of what we currently use to do our work and if you start working with us you'll have the opportunity to learn and work with them as well. What You Can Expect: If you work with us you'll get clear project specs that detail what the end goals are -- how something needs to work -- and realistic expectations for delivering it. You'll have direct communication with our in-house development team and timely responses to any questions. You'll get prompt payment and have the opportunity for bonuses based on meeting goals. IMPORTANT: You MUST be able to provide examples of your code, not just links to sites you have worked on. We understand that prior work may be confidential and can't be provided in full but code samples from a project that demonstrate your proficiency and approach are extremely important. Please provide links to your Github/GitLab profile or open source projects you contributed to and/or any other representative examples of your work that are relevant to the position. If you are active in communities like StackOverflow, please let us know as well

title: Public Survey to assess perceptions of Longevity / Healthspan Science and Research
description: VitaDAO is a global community of longevity enthusiasts, researchers, and contributors working to identify, fund, and incubate research in longevity science. In the past year we have funded more than 15 ageing research projects and initiatives, sponsored multiple longevity conferences, and provided travel grants to early-stage researchers. We invite you to explore our website at https://www.vitadao.com/. As part of of 2023 strategic plan we are endeavoring to tackle a messaging problem - legitimate longevity science driven by highly accomplished Ph.D. researchers is being intermixed with social media and fad "experts" and non-verifiable science. This, we believe is making it difficult for the general public to appreciate the work being done in the longevity science space. Additionally the marketing of supplements, cremes, and a number of cosmetic "therapies" many of which are of questionable effect, are diluting and in some cases outright discrediting the field. We seek to regain control of the narrative and give the general public an honest view of the science that is happening right now in the space focused on improved healthspan and ultimately lifespan. As part of this process, and recognizing that those within our eco-system are already sold on the benefits of longevity science we need to establish how best to communicate outward to the general public about the field of longevity research. This first survey is to be designed (and will be implemented in SurveyMonkey) with the goal of identifying the concerns/blockers of the general public towards extending lifespan through science. Examples of some of the arguments against this kind of research that we often get are: •Overpopulation / Resource Scarcity, •The notion that aging must lead to poor health and frailty, •Preventing death isn't moral or "natural". We need to establish both the policy concerns, but also looking for insight on how to make the topic personally relevant. This job is to design the survey which will then be implemented using the SurveyMonkey service by our team. . We are looking for expertise in question development/answer format to help us formulate our strategy.
